abstract: Lamport logical clocks provide a total order on distributed events but do not encode causal relationships. We investigate how a balanced search and indexing structure can expose the "Lamport Timestamp Trap" where ordered numbers fail to reflect causality. A lightweight Chronos-Interpreter implementation is presented that augments a classic Lamport clock with a height-balanced tree to maintain event indices. We prove that the tree preserves the strict height-balanced invariant while the timestamp ordering remains total but not causal. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V45 system shows a mean latency of 31 315.10 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 31 934 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_140125_the_lamport_timestamp_trap__or}
